findings.reason: the reuse premise for the cache is false, so the section must either state that the sha-keyed cache is a distinct mechanism that stays on the counter, or name the velocity helper it actually intends.
findings.text: §10's reuse map names an owner that does not exist: it says "the revision-keyed cache helpers ... stay on velocity, stay private, and are imported by the counter", but velocity's only cache helpers are `_velocity_cache_path`/`_load_captured_history`/`_store_captured_history` (keyed by repository path, holding a captured-history window) and `_ledger_cache_path`/`_load_ledger_cache`/`_store_ledger_cache`; none is revision-keyed, and the counter's sha-keyed cache (`reckon/interface_counts.py:503-538`) is the only revision-keyed cache in the package. A worker implementing the section literally has nothing on velocity to import for that half

findings.reason: the section should share the tokenisation rule that is genuinely duplicated (`token_lines`/`docstring_spans`) and leave the interface-shape predicates (`definitions`, `interfaces`) with the counter that owns them, rather than gathering six leaf functions into a left-overs module.
findings.text: the proposed "one module named for what they do" is a bundle of two unrelated mechanisms that share no importer: `interface_counts` uses `definitions`, `call_name`, `literal_strings` and `interfaces`, while `clones` uses only `token_lines` and `docstring_spans` — the two consumers import disjoint halves, and the plan's own premise that "one normalisation rule now lives in three places" is true for `token_lines` alone, which `interface_counts` never calls. A module whose name cannot be one capability, because it holds six, adds surface without hiding shared behaviour

findings.reason: the owning file is `reckon/velocity.py`, and the honest change is to promote the blob reader and cache root there to a stable (non-underscore) name the counter imports, so the shared mechanism has a public home instead of a private one.
findings.text: the repair has the counter import velocity's underscore-private helper (`_velocity_cache_root`, already reached at `reckon/interface_counts.py:498` via the module-private `_cache_root`) and the plan says every lifted velocity helper "keeps its leading underscore and is never counted"; a cross-module import of a `_`-name keeps the shared mechanism private, makes the counter's dependency on velocity invisible to the interface counts, and repeats the very fork-hidden-in-a-private-helper pattern this plan exists to remove

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the single "module named for what they do" bundles six leaf predicates whose two consumers import disjoint halves, so it hides no shared behaviour and adds a module of surface without depth.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the repair reaches the counter into velocity's underscore-private helpers (as `interface_counts._cache_root` already reaches for `velocity._velocity_cache_root`, `reckon/velocity.py:521`) instead of promoting the shared mechanism on its owner's interface, so the shared machinery stays private and uncounted.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — the section accounts for its own surface: the four public predicate names move to the new module and are retired from the counter, so public_definitions does not grow, and every lifted velocity helper keeps its leading underscore.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §10 asserts velocity already owns the "revision-keyed cache" the counter re-implements, but velocity's cache helpers are keyed by repository path and hold a captured-history window, while the only sha-keyed cache is the counter's own `_cache_path`/`_load_cached`/`_store_cached` in `reckon/interface_counts.py:503-538`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the extraction of velocity's `cat-file --batch` loop into one private helper is an extension of the mechanism that already exists in `velocity._plan_metas`, not a parallel layer, and the plan says why the census copy cannot be the runtime owner.
